is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates Anopheles arabiensis, An. coluzzii, and An. gambiae (page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports the L1014F kdr mutation (Vgsc L995F) (page 1, 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 (page 4) provides the number of specimens (n) and the L1014F allele frequency for each of the 20 sites and three species.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from 20 sites in the Tambacounda region of southeastern Senegal (page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study investigating kdr frequencies and insecticide susceptibility (page 1).

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is reported for 20 specific sites in the Tambacounda region, including coordinates in Figure 1 and site names in Table 1.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected during the rainy seasons of 2010 and 2011 (page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes original field collections in Senegal funded by the INFRAVEC project; there is no indication that this is a subset of a larger published dataset like Ag1000G.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype frequencies and sample sizes are contained within the main text and Table 1.

assessment.summary: This study investigated the frequency of the Vgsc L1014F (kdr-west) mutation in sympatric populations of Anopheles arabiensis, An. coluzzii, and An. gambiae across 20 sites in the Tambacounda region of Senegal. Collections were conducted in 2010 (indoor resting adults via PSC) and 2011 (larvae for bioassays). The study provides site-specific allele frequencies and sample sizes for all three species across both transects.
